correctness.rationale: By structural induction, rank-d child formulas see only exact sizes 0..2^d and one tail. For n>2^(d+1), a pair of exact child types cannot merge to n, while every pair containing a tail is realized (including at infinite n); exact n is independent of its ambient set. Characteristic formulas recover every size up to 2^(d+1) using the union-size interval and subtraction of previously recovered sizes. This proves both directions, all quantifiers, and the sharp depth statement, separately from the finite checks. Direct powerset evaluation matched cardinality abstraction in 35,770 cases and formula characterizers passed 9,709 cases.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source introduces and analyzes a binary supremum modal language over semilattices, but inspected Sections 2–4 and appendix treat translations and richer operators, not the sharp depth-bounded fixed empty/singleton pointed-cardinality classification. The 2025 full HTML treats undecidability under arbitrary valuations. The 2023 treatment is of preorders/posets and defers semilattices. Full text of a related published first-order Boolean-algebra rank theorem was compared: its quantifier rank and full Boolean-operation language neither directly imply the present binary modal cutoff nor the semantic Boolean algebra of formula types. Related bisimulation and Boolean quantifier-elimination results remain a plausible priority risk; the comparison is best-knowledge, not uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: Binary union is the core information-fusion modality in new and established modal information logic. Its fixed zero and singleton observations describe a canonical natural no-parameter fragment on powersets. The theorem gives a complete sharp depth hierarchy, exact pointed-type and formula equivalence counts, and an effective normal form, including a finite representative for every infinite information state at bounded depth. It characterizes a structural expressivity boundary, not a routine single finite instance or arbitrary slice; it makes no overclaim for richer syntax.
